public_observations.topic: AI CFD Scientist verifier ablation revision binding
public_observations.observation: The public ablation driver and quick interpreter both have a pre-submission repository revision at commit 4702512117b1fbaa4cb50de7787c288877c5812f dated 2026-05-06, one day before arXiv:2605.06607 submission. At that revision, run_vlm_ablation.py already declares the exact 20-case design (16 planted failures plus 4 controls), copies previously PROCEED'd production cases, applies one post-hoc perturbation, renders interpret-mode figures, and calls the single-shot verifier. The pre-submission quick_interpret.py maps verdict status from rerun_required alone: requirement_met and simulation_success are parsed but do not control PROCEED/REVISE/RERUN, and there is no HOLD/UNINSPECTABLE disposition. This materially strengthens mechanism provenance for the reported ablation relative to inspecting only current main, while still not proving the paper's executed runs were generated from this exact commit without an explicit run-to-commit binding.
public_observations.boundary: pre-submission mechanism lineage is strong but not a certified run-to-commit provenance binding

public_observations.topic: AI CFD Scientist post-submission deterministic stage audit
public_observations.observation: The current public stage_gate_audit.py is a post-submission hardening layer first appearing on 2026-05-20, after the 2026-05-07 paper submission. It deterministically enforces predecessor checkpoints, honest run-result status, retry exhaustion for failed production cases, solver-log completion, presence of figs/, decision.json, and a vision-pass anti-bypass string check. However its per-case gate requires only at least one PNG plus a decision artifact; it does not bind each scientific requirement to the exact evidence visible to the VLM, nor does it validate a requirement-specific evidence coverage manifest. Thus deterministic terminal verification and verifier evidence observability are separable concerns. The stage audit is useful current implementation evidence but cannot be credited as part of the reported pre-submission ablation mechanism.
public_observations.boundary: post-submission implementation pattern, not evaluated-paper mechanism

public_observations.observation: Additional public search surfaced science/data-science memory-on/off studies and quality-controlled case memory, including CBR-augmented R&D-Agent, but did not surface a matched ablation that isolates receiver-side applicability/revalidation of transferred failure memory itself. The CBR study compares the whole CBR layer against disabled baseline and describes a five-gate retention filter/reuse heuristic; it does not isolate a target-side adoption/revalidation gate. Therefore the direct causal frontier remains open.
public_observations.boundary: whole-memory-layer ablation is not target-side revalidation ablation

protocol_inferences.name: VERIFIER_OBSERVABILITY_SCOPE_v2
protocol_inferences.rule: Hard negative verification requires complete declared evidence coverage plus falsifying evidence that is cryptographically bound to a declared requirement and exactly matches the artifact digest visible to the verifier. A stale, unseen, or out-of-scope falsifying artifact cannot authorize REJECT/BLOCK/PRUNE/FORBID. Evidence-requirement or visible-evidence digest drift invalidates cached verification.

protocol_inferences.name: terminal_audit_vs_epistemic_coverage
protocol_inferences.rule: Deterministic lifecycle audits can establish that required stages/artifacts/log conditions exist without establishing that a semantic verifier had sufficient claim-specific evidence. Handoff protocols should model terminal/lifecycle validity and verifier observability coverage as separate inspectable dimensions.
